info.title: RealEstateAPI Documentation
info.description:
RealEstateAPI provides property data, MLS listings, skip trace, and utility services.

Endpoints are grouped by product below.

## Common Workflows

- **Property Search → Detail:** Use /v2/PropertySearch to find properties, then /v2/PropertyDetail with the returned 'id' for full details.
- **Property Valuation:** Use /v2/PropertyAvm for a single valuation, or /v2/PropertyAvmBulk for up to 100 properties.
- **Comparable Sales:** Use /v3/PropertyComps with a property id or address to get comparable sales, an AVM range, and the subject property's own record.
- **Skip Trace:** Use /v2/SkipTrace with a property address or a name to find associated people and contact information.
- **MLS Listings:** Use /v3/MLSSearch (full filter set, compound and/or, field selection), /v3/MLSDetail or /v3/MLSDetailBulk for full records, /v3/MLSPropertyMapping for map pins, and /v3/MLSBoardCoverage for board coverage by state/zip/county/city.
- **Bulk Operations:** Use /v2/PropertyDetailBulk (up to 1000 IDs) or /v2/SkipTraceBatch (up to 1000 records).
- **Data Discovery:** Use /v2/AutoComplete or /v3/AutoComplete for address/city/zip suggestions. Use GET /v2/key/info to see your available endpoints.

## Authentication

All endpoints require an `x-api-key` header. Use GET /v2/key/info to discover your available scopes and rate limits.

tags.name: Property Data
tags.description: Public-record property data: search with 100+ filters across the national property universe, pull full property detail (ownership, mortgages, tax, sales history, foreclosure, demographics), drop map pins, and export result sets to CSV.

tags.name: Valuation & Comps
tags.description: Automated valuations (AVM) for one or many properties, and comparable-sales analysis with a comps-derived AVM range.

tags.name: MLS
tags.description: MLS listing data (v3): search active, pending, sold and off-market listings, pull full listing records, render map pins, autocomplete MLS addresses, and look up which boards cover a market. Requires an MLS-enabled plan.

tags.name: MLS (v2)
tags.description: The original v2 MLS endpoints; each one names its v3 replacement. New integrations should start on the MLS (v3) endpoints above.

tags.name: Skip Trace
tags.description: Find the people associated with a property or a name and return their phones, emails, social profiles and demographics. Single, synchronous batch, and asynchronous (webhook) batch flavors.

tags.name: Address & AutoComplete
tags.description: Type-ahead suggestions for addresses, streets, cities, counties, zips and APNs, and bulk matching of free-form addresses to RealEstateAPI property IDs.

tags.name: Property Data (OData)
tags.description: OData v4 access to Property Search, so standard OData and RESO tooling (Power BI, Excel, RESO Web API clients) can query property data without custom code.

tags.name: Bulk Data Files
tags.description: Daily change files for customers who mirror the property dataset locally.

tags.name: Account
tags.description: Introspect your API key: scopes, available endpoints and rate limits.

sale_since_last_mls_status.description: Whether the property has sold since its latest MLS status. A sale is either the listing closing (mlsStatus Closed) or a deed-recorded sale on or after the latest MLS status date (lastSaleDate >= mlsLastStatusDate), so off-MLS sales count and a recent MLS closing counts even before the deed is recorded. true selects properties that have sold since. false selects everything else: properties whose latest status is not Closed and with no recorded sale since that status (never sold, or sold before it) - e.g. expired, cancelled, or withdrawn listings not sold since they failed - and properties with no MLS history at all (never listed). true and false together cover every property. Active and Pending listings satisfy false (not sold yet); exclude those statuses with mls_last_status if you want off-market inventory only.

remove_prefix_duplicates.description: Opt-in (default false). Some MLS boards switched to feeds that prefix every MLS ID with a board code (e.g. IRES 881767 -> IRE881767). The feed re-issued existing listings under the prefixed number as new records and left the bare record behind, often marked Closed while the prefixed record is current. With true, an mls_number or *_mls_code search removes a bare record when its prefixed twin from the same board is also in the results, so each listing appears once, as its current record. The prefixed record is always kept, regardless of status or modification date: the bare twin's status and timestamp come from the retired feed and are not reliable. Very large lookups may be only partly de-duplicated: pairing covers up to 30,000 distinct MLS numbers per board (60,000 when one mls_board_code is sent). v2 does not report how many records were removed or when that limit is reached (v3 MLSSearch does, in warnings). Costs one extra query, skipped when the requested boards never switched.

MLSSearchV3Sort.description: Sort: { "<field>": "asc"|"desc" }. Accepts any sortable v3 field path (e.g. "listingPrice", "address.zip") or a v2 sort name (e.g. "listing_date"). Unsortable fields return INVALID_SORT_FIELD with a suggestion. isSold is sortable on any search. closeDate (aliases soldDate, sold_date, close_date) sorts only when the search asserts the sold group — sold: true, status "Sold" alone (not mixed with other statuses), a sold_* filter or has_sold_price: true, at the top level or in an `and` item — and closePrice (aliases soldPrice, sold_price, close_price) when it asserts the sold or the closed group (or has_close_price: true); outside those groups the response value is resolved at read time with no indexed column, so the sort returns INVALID_SORT_FIELD with the fix. Listings with no value sort last. Fields computed per record at read time (daysOnMarket, pricePerSquareFoot) are not sortable; for listing age on Active, Pending and Active Under Contract listings, sort on listingContractDate (desc = fewest days on market). Sorting on public.* requires public-record access; otherwise returns 403 PUBLIC_RECORD_SORT_FORBIDDEN. Applies identically on MLSPropertyMapping, where it decides which pins a page holds.

get.description:
OData v4 front end to /v2/PropertySearch for standard OData and RESO tooling (Power BI, Excel, RESO Web API clients). Filter with `$filter` (e.g. `address/city eq 'Austin'`), page with `$top` (up to 1,000) and `$skip`, sort with `$orderby`, project fields with `$select`, and add `$count=true` for the total.

With no query options at all, returns the OData service document instead of data. Requires the PropertySearch scope; data pages are metered, the service document is not.

post.summary: Match up to 100 addresses to RealEstateAPI properties in one request
post.description:
Resolves a list of `addresses` (up to 100) to properties in the RealEstateAPI dataset and returns, per address, the RealEstateAPI property `id`, the standardized property address (with ZIP+4, carrier route and congressional district), the owner mailing address, APN, latitude/longitude, vacant and absentee-owner flags, and the match `confidence` and `precision`.

Each item can be a full `address` string, address components (`street`, `city`, `state`, `zip`), or an `apn` with `fips` — or an `id`. Matches below a confidence of 0.87 are returned as misses rather than guessed. `strict` (default true) controls how tightly the address must match; `address_range_check: true` lets a single house number resolve to a hyphenated range parcel (4053 → 4051-4055). Include a `key` on each item to match results back to your records.

Typical use: clean a lead list, then pass the returned IDs to /v2/PropertyDetailBulk.

post.summary: Type-ahead suggestions for addresses, streets, cities, counties, zips and APNs
post.description:
Returns ranked suggestions for partial input in `search` (2+ characters) — built for search boxes. Each suggestion carries the identifiers you need for the next call, e.g. the property `id` for an address suggestion to send to /v2/PropertyDetail, or the city / zip / county values to send to /v2/PropertySearch.

- `search_types`: limit suggestions to one or more types — A (address), S (street), C (city), N (county), G (neighborhood), Z (zip), P (APN), T (state).
- `latitude` / `longitude` (+ `precision` 1–10): bias results toward a location, e.g. the user's map view.

For property and MLS suggestions in one call, use /v3/AutoComplete.

post.summary: Get download links for the property change files published on a given date
post.description:
For customers who keep a local copy of the property dataset in sync. Send a `file_date` (YYYY-MM-DD) and receive every change file published that day: file name, size, last-modified time and a pre-signed `downloadUrl` that expires one hour after the request (`expiresAt`).

When no files were published for the date the HTTP status is still 200 and the body carries `statusCode: 404`, an empty `data` object and a `reason`; check the body, not the transport status. Requires the ChangeFiles scope.

- `file_name`: optional name for the file (5–60 characters).
- `map`: optional column layout as `"Header:field.path"` strings, e.g. `"city:propertyInfo.address.city"`; defaults to a standard owner, address and property layout.
- `webcomplete_url`: optional URL notified when the file is ready.
- `count: true` returns the match count only, without building a file.

post.summary: Search the national property dataset with 100+ filters
post.description:
Find properties by location — full `address`, `city`, `county`, `state`, `zip` (one or many), a `latitude`/`longitude` + `radius`, or a `polygon` / `multi_polygon` — and narrow them with 100+ filters covering ownership (absentee, corporate, trust, out-of-state), equity and mortgages, sale history, MLS status, pre-foreclosure / auction / REO and other distress signals, building characteristics, tax and census data.

- **Paging:** up to 250 results per page via `size`; continue with `resultIndex`.
- **Modes:** `count: true` returns only the total match count; `ids_only: true` returns up to 10,000 property IDs in a single call (`size`/`resultIndex` are ignored); `summary: true` adds lead-type counts for the result set.

post.summary: Search properties in plain English (beta)
post.description:
Describe the properties you want in natural language — e.g. "3 bed homes in Austin TX under $400k with a pool owned more than 10 years" — and PropGPT translates the request into a /v2/PropertySearch query, runs it, and returns the results.

post.summary: Skip trace one person: phones, emails, demographics and address history
post.description:
Finds the person behind a property, a mailing address, a name, a phone number or an email address, and returns their contact details (phone numbers, email addresses, social profiles), demographics (age, gender, marital status, ethnicity, occupation), and current and previous addresses.

**Ways to search** — send at least one of `address`, `mail_address`, `city`, `mail_city`, `zip`, `mail_zip`, `email` or `phone`:

- **Property address:** `address` + `city` + `state` (`zip` and `unit` optional). Add `first_name`/`last_name` to pick a specific owner.
- **Mailing address:** the same, with the `mail_*` fields.
- **Name + area:** `first_name` + `last_name` with a zip, or a city plus a state or zip.
- **Reverse lookup:** `phone` (10 digits, no formatting) or `email`.

**Options**

- `match_requirements`: only count a person as a match when they have phones and/or emails (pass `operator` when requiring more than one).
- Demographic filters (`age` or `age_range_min`/`age_range_max`, `gender`, `marital_status_code`, `ethnicity_code`, `occupation_code`) narrow name and area searches; all but age need a zip or a city and state.
- `key`: a pass-through value echoed back in the response.

For lists, use /v2/SkipTraceBatchAwait (synchronous) or /v2/SkipTraceBatch (asynchronous with webhooks).

post.summary: Queue up to 1,000 skip traces and receive the results by webhook
post.description:
Asynchronous batch skip trace. Send `skips`, a list of 1–1,000 /v2/SkipTrace request bodies (256 KB maximum payload), and a `webcomplete_url`. The call returns immediately with a `batchRequestId` per skip and a `receiveCount`; the skips are processed in the background.

Results are delivered by webhook: a skip that carries its own `webhook_url` has its result posted there, and `webcomplete_url` is notified when the whole batch has finished. Include a `key` on each skip to match results back to your records.

Use this for large lists; for up to about 100 records where you want the results in the response, use /v2/SkipTraceBatchAwait.

post.summary: Skip trace a list of people and get every result back in the response
post.description:
Synchronous batch skip trace. Send `skips`, a list of /v2/SkipTrace request bodies (256 KB maximum payload), and the request stays open until every record has been processed; the response returns one result per skip.

Each skip accepts the same address, name, phone and email search options and `match_requirements` as /v2/SkipTrace. Include a `key` on each skip to match results back to your records.

Best for small batches of up to about 100 records. For larger lists, use /v2/SkipTraceBatch, which processes in the background and delivers results by webhook.

post.summary: Unified property and MLS type-ahead suggestions
post.description:
One autocomplete for both datasets. Returns address, street, city, county, zip, state, neighborhood, APN and MLS board suggestions for partial input in `search`. When an address exists in MLS data, the MLS suggestion replaces the public-record one, so each address appears once; fields a suggestion does not have are returned as null.

- `search_types`: A (address, the default), S (street), C (city), N (county), Z (zip), T (state), B (MLS board), P (APN, property only), G (neighborhood, property only).
- `latitude` / `longitude` (+ `precision` 1–10) bias results toward a location.

MLS suggestions require the MLS scope and an MLS plan; without them, you get property suggestions only. Not metered.

post.summary: MLS type-ahead suggestions for addresses, streets, places and boards
post.description:
Returns suggestions for partial input in `search`, drawn from MLS data: listing addresses and streets, and MLS boards; cities, counties, zips and states are resolved as places.

- `search_types`: A (address, the default), S (street), C (city), N (county), Z (zip), B (MLS board), T (state).
- `latitude` / `longitude` (+ `precision` 1–10) bias results toward a location.

Free for any key with an active MLS plan (not metered). For property and MLS suggestions in one call, use /v3/AutoComplete.

post.summary: Look up which MLS boards cover a state, zip, county or city
post.description:
A reference lookup for planning MLS work — not a listing search; no listing data is returned. Pick a `mode` and a `state` scope (required, up to 5 states):

- `boards`: the board catalog — code, display name, states served and listing count — in one response. `group_by_state: true` reshapes it per state; `show_all: true` keeps states and boards with no active listings.
- `zips`, `counties`, `cities`: every zip, county or city in scope paired with the board(s) that cover it, paged with `size` (up to 2,000) and the `next_cursor` from the previous response.

Use it to decide which `mls_board_code` values to sync or filter on in /v3/MLSSearch.

post.summary: Get the full v3 record for one MLS listing
post.description:
Retrieves one MLS listing by any of: `listing_id`, `public_id` (RealEstateAPI property ID), `apn`, an `address` (full string or components), or `mls_number` with `mls_board_code`. If several are sent, the first in this order wins: mls_number → listing_id → public_id → apn → address.

The record covers price and status history, agents and offices, rooms and features, open houses, schools, media and remarks. Trim it with `fields` (dot-path allowlist) or `field_sections`, and add the linked public-record block with `public: true` (requires a public-record plan).

For many listings at once, use /v3/MLSDetailBulk. Requires an MLS plan.

post.summary: Get full v3 MLS records for up to 1,000 listings in one request
post.description:
Retrieves many listings at once by `listing_ids` (internal MLS listing IDs) or `public_ids` (RealEstateAPI property IDs) — one list or the other, up to 1,000 IDs. Each record has the same shape and the same `fields` / `field_sections` / `public` options as /v3/MLSDetail.

Results come back in request order with a per-item outcome: an ID that is missing (or null) yields an error object at its position instead of failing the request. Set `verbose: true` to add lookup context and a hint to each error.

Pairs with the `listing_ids_only` / `ids_only` modes of /v3/MLSSearch. Requires an MLS plan.

post.summary: Get map pins for every MLS listing matching a v3 search
post.description:
Accepts the full /v3/MLSSearch request body — every filter, plus `count`, `size` (up to 10,000 here), `resultIndex` and `sort` — and returns one lightweight point per match: `listingId`, `publicId`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `listingPrice`, `status`, `listingPropertyType` and `listingDate`. That is enough to render, label and style a marker without a follow-up call. `sort` behaves as on /v3/MLSSearch: no sort orders by `modificationTimestamp` descending, and a radius search with no sort returns nearest first.

**One pin per property by default.** `latest_only` is true here unless you send `latest_only: false` (multi-family properties can then carry one pin per unit), so `resultCount` counts properties and no client-side de-duplication is needed. This is the one deliberate difference from /v3/MLSSearch, which defaults to every listing — send `latest_only: true` there to compare totals.

The record-shaping options (`fields`, `field_sections`, `public`, `public_ids_only`, `ids_only`, `listing_ids_only`, `include_photos`, `obfuscate`, `summary`) are accepted but have no effect — the response is always the fixed point shape, and each one sent is echoed in `warnings[]`.

`resultIndex` pages past Elasticsearch's 10,000-result window transparently; result sets over 100,000 listings refuse `resultIndex` > 0 with a 416 (RESULT_SET_TOO_LARGE_TO_PAGE) — narrow the search, or page by `modification_timestamp_min` instead. Requires an MLS plan.

post.summary: Search MLS listings with the full v3 filter set
post.description:
Searches MLS listings — active, pending, sold and off-market — across every board on your plan, with 270+ filters, boolean logic and a response field selector.

**Filters**

- **Location:** address components, `city` / `state` / `zip` / `county`, `mls_board_code`, `latitude` + `longitude` + `radius`, or a `polygon` / `multi_polygon`.
- **Listing:** `status` (or the `active` / `pending` / `sold` shortcuts), property type and sub-type, `*_min` / `*_max` ranges for price, dates, beds, baths, living area, lot size and year built.
- **People:** listing, selling, co-listing and co-selling agent and office by name, email, phone or MLS code.
- **Features:** pool, garage, views, waterfront, HOA, open houses, photos, new construction, green features, keywords in the public remarks, and more.
- **Public record:** `public_*` filters on the linked public-record property (absentee owner, vacancy, corporate ownership, ...).

**Logic, modes and paging**

- Combine criteria with compound `and` / `or` groups (`minimum_or_matches` for "at least N of"), and negate any filter with `exclude`.
- `count: true` returns the total only; `public_ids_only` (alias `ids_only`) returns property IDs (`publicId`, counted and paged as `has_public_id: true`) and `listing_ids_only` returns MLS listing IDs; the two cannot be combined.
- Results include every listing by default; `latest_only: true` keeps only each property's latest listing (drops relists and cross-board duplicates).
- Page with `size` (default 50, max 250) and `resultIndex`; sort with `sort: { "<field>": "asc" | "desc" }` on any sortable field.
- Shape the response with `fields` (dot-path allowlist) or `field_sections`; add the public-record block with `public: true` (requires a public-record plan).

Send the same body to /v3/MLSPropertyMapping for map pins, and pass a result's `listingId` to /v3/MLSDetail for the full record. Requires an MLS plan.

post.summary: Get comparable sales, a comps-based AVM range, and the subject property record
post.description:
Finds recently sold properties comparable to a subject property — identified by RealEstateAPI `id` or a full `address` — and returns them in `comps` along with a valuation (`reapiAvm`, `reapiAvmLow`, `reapiAvmHigh`) and the subject property's own detail record in `subject`, so one request covers both the comps and the property.

**Tuning the comp set**

- Search area and recency: `max_radius_miles`, `max_days_back`.
- Hard filters: living and lot square-feet, last sale price and MLS listing price ranges, plus `same_*` switches (county, zip, census tract, neighborhood, subdivision, beds, baths, construction type) and `arms_length`.
- Similarity weighting: the `*_boost` parameters (1–50) raise the importance of living area, lot size, bedrooms, bathrooms or year built when ranking candidates.
- `max_results` caps the number of comps returned.

When the default search area finds too few comps, it retries once with a wider radius and longer look-back; `fallback` reports both attempts (null when no retry was needed). Requires a Growth plan or above. Replaces /v2/PropertyComps and the deprecated `comps` option on /v2/PropertyDetail.

Close (sale) price of THIS listing, from the MLS via the pipeline. Set on every sold listing (isSold): where the MLS reports no close price it is the list price, and closeDataSource is "mls_list_price" (dataAssumptions.soldPriceDerived). Null on listings that are not sold or closed. On listings not yet carrying the pipeline fields it is derived at read time from the same listing on an overlapping MLS board (closeDataSource "linked_mls_listing"). NOT public.lastSaleAmount, which is the parcel's most recent recorded deed and often a different sale.

isSold.description: true when the listing is a sale under the pipeline's rules: Closed with a close price, or the MLS-internal status "Sold". A Pending listing is never sold. Exactly the listings sold: true and status "Sold" return. Null on listings not yet carrying the pipeline fields.

This is the date sold_date_* and closed_date_* filter on. Never sourced from public.lastSaleDate (a different transaction).

"mls_list_price" = a sale the MLS reported without a close price; closePrice is the list price. "mls_status_history" = the MLS status change into the listing's current status (date only). "mls_status_change_timestamp" = the listing's last status-change timestamp (date only). "mls_last_modified" = the listing's last modification, when no status date exists (date only, approximate). On listings not yet carrying the pipeline fields: "linked_mls_listing" = this listing's counterpart on an overlapping MLS board (price and date); "mls_dom_computed" = listingContractDate + daysOnMarket (date only, approximate).
